title: Audit Record Review, Analysis & Cross-Source Correlation (CUI)
exclusions: This is the CMMC AU.L2-3.3.5 audit review/analysis and cross-source correlation control for the CUI environment. It correlates different audit-event categories for the same actor across sources to surface activity that no single log shows. It does NOT cover audit-record generation/collection (AU.L2-3.3.1 / UC-22.35.6), log protection/integrity (AU.L2-3.3.8), or response. Service accounts are scoped via the actor allowlist.
evidence: Saved search 'UC-22.20.22 — audit correlation (CUI)' runs on the review cadence, writes each correlated-actor record to the restricted audit_evidence index, and feeds the 'CUI audit correlation' dashboard — the dated evidence a C3PAO assessor reads to confirm AU.L2-3.3.5 review and correlation operate.

compliance.assurance_rationale: AU.L2-3.3.5 requires correlating audit record review, analysis and reporting processes for investigation of and response to indications of unlawful, unauthorized, suspicious or unusual activity. This UC implements that correlation directly: it normalises audit events from every source into categories (failed access, privilege change, configuration change) and surfaces actors exhibiting two or more categories within a window — the cross-source correlation the practice calls for — as a dated review record. Splunk is the sole-sufficient mechanism that performs and evidences the correlated review, so the grade is full.
compliance.controlObjective: Proves AU.L2-3.3.5 operates — audit records from multiple sources are correlated per actor and review-worthy multi-category activity is surfaced and reported for the CUI environment.
compliance.evidenceArtifact: Saved search 'UC-22.20.22' correlated-actor records archived to the restricted audit_evidence index for C3PAO review.

controlTest.positiveScenario: For one account, generate a failed-access cluster and, within the same window, a privilege-change event (e.g. add to an admin group) on a different host/source. On the next run the account appears with distinct_event_types>=2 and event_types containing both 'failed_access' and 'privilege_change', and the correlated record is archived to audit_evidence.
controlTest.negativeScenario: During normal operation where actors generate at most one audit-event category in the window, the search yields no rows (distinct_event_types<2) and the period is recorded as a clean correlated review.

dataSources: All in-scope CUI-environment audit sources carrying an actor field across access, privilege and configuration domains (e.g. `WinEventLog:Security`, `linux_secure`, endpoint/EDR audit, directory and configuration-management logs). Optional `audit_review_allowlist.csv` scopes service accounts.
app: Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform (native). Splunk Enterprise Security recommended for notable/risk correlation in the CUI enclave.
spl:
index=* sourcetype=* (action=* OR status=* OR signature=*) earliest=-24h
| eval evt=case(match(coalesce(action,status,signature),"(?i)fail|denied|lockout"), "failed_access", match(coalesce(action,signature),"(?i)privilege|escalat|sudo|role|group add|added to|admin"), "privilege_change", match(coalesce(action,signature),"(?i)config|policy|registry|gpo|baseline"), "config_change", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(evt) AND isnotnull(user) AND user!="" AND user!="-"
| stats count as events, dc(evt) as distinct_event_types, values(evt) as event_types, values(sourcetype) as sourcetypes, dc(host) as hosts, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by user
| where distinct_event_types>=2
| eval correlation_window_min=round((last_seen-first_seen)/60, 1)
| eval correlated_at=strftime(now(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
| table correlated_at, user, event_types, distinct_event_types, events, hosts, sourcetypes, correlation_window_min
| sort - distinct_event_types, - events
description: Operates the CMMC AU.L2-3.3.5 correlation practice: it normalises audit events from every in-scope source into categories (failed access, privilege change, configuration change) and surfaces any actor exhibiting two or more categories within a time window — the multi-source correlation that reveals activity no single log shows — as a dated, analyst-ready review record.
value: Single-log review misses the actor who fails to log in, then is granted privilege, then changes a configuration — each event looks benign alone. This control correlates those categories per actor across sources, giving the assessor dated evidence that correlated review operates and giving the SOC a high-signal lead. One scheduled search satisfies the CMMC correlation practice for the CUI environment.
implementation: (1) Ensure access, privilege and configuration audit sources for the CUI enclave carry a normalised `user` field; (2) maintain audit_review_allowlist.csv for service accounts; (3) schedule on the review cadence (e.g. hourly correlation with a daily roll-up); (4) route correlated rows to the restricted audit_evidence index and (where ES is present) raise a notable; (5) extend the category regexes to match your audit vocabulary. Indexes required: all in-scope CUI audit indexes; Lookups: audit_review_allowlist.csv.
visualization: Table (user, event_types, distinct_event_types, correlation_window_min) with multi-category rows highlighted; single-value 'correlated actors (24h)'; column chart of correlated actors by category mix. Key fields: `user`, `event_types`, `distinct_event_types`.

references.title: CMMC 2.0 — AU.L2-3.3.5 Audit Record Review, Analysis and Reporting
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — AU-6 (basis for CMMC AU.L2-3.3.5)

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Administrators doing legitimate work** — A sysadmin may legitimately authenticate, change a role and edit a configuration in one window; correlate with the change-ticket lookup before treating as a finding.

2. **Service / automation accounts** — Orchestration tools touch multiple categories routinely; list them in audit_review_allowlist.csv.

3. **Category over-match** — Broad regexes can mis-categorise an event; tune the category patterns to your audit vocabulary during rollout.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain audit_review_allowlist.csv and (optionally) a change-window lookup; allowlisted actors and approved-change windows are annotated and excluded from alerting while remaining in the analysed evidence.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Enterprise ≥9.2 or Splunk Cloud; Splunk Enterprise Security recommended for the CUI enclave so correlated actors become notables.
• **Normalised actor field** across access, privilege and configuration sources (FIELDALIAS to `user`).
• **Category coverage**: at least two of the three event categories (failed access, privilege change, configuration change) must be onboarded for correlation to be meaningful.
• **Allowlist**: `audit_review_allowlist.csv` (column `user`).
• **Evidence index**: restricted `audit_evidence` with CUI-appropriate access controls and retention.
• **Regulatory mapping**: evidences CMMC `AU.L2-3.3.5`. Every result carries `event_types` and `correlated_at`.

## Step 1 — Define the audit categories

AU.L2-3.3.5 is about *correlation*, so the control's value depends on the category mapping. Review the `eval evt=case(...)` patterns against your actual audit vocabulary; add patterns for any access/privilege/configuration event types specific to your estate. Keep the three-category model so the `distinct_event_types>=2` correlation stays interpretable.

## Step 2 — Implement the search

The search categorises every audit event, then `stats ... by user` collapses an actor's window into the set of categories they touched and the time span. The `where distinct_event_types>=2` is the correlation gate. Schedule it:

```ini
[UC-22.20.22: Audit Record Review, Analysis & Cross-Source Correlation (CUI)]
cron_schedule = 15 * * * *
dispatch.earliest_time = -24h
dispatch.latest_time = now
actions = summary_index
action.summary_index._name = audit_evidence
action.summary_index.marker = uc=22.20.22,controls=AU.L2-3.3.5
```

## Step 3 — Validate

Run the positive test (one actor, two categories) and confirm a correlated row; run the negative test (single-category activity) and confirm zero rows. Confirm allowlisted service accounts are excluded.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Build 'CUI audit correlation': single-value correlated-actor count, a correlated-actor table, and a category-mix chart. Schedule the evidence export to audit_evidence on the review cadence for C3PAO review.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting and caveats

• **Everything correlates:** category regexes are over-broad — tighten them.

• **Nothing correlates:** confirm at least two categories are onboarded and the actor field resolves across them.

• **Scope discipline:** reconcile categories against the CUI audit-source inventory so correlation coverage is complete.
grandmaExplanation: We watch for people whose activity ties together across different systems — like someone who fails to log in, then suddenly gets extra access, then changes a setting. Any one of those alone looks fine, so we connect the dots and keep a dated note for the auditor.
